report.tagline: A caller ID and spam-blocking app that tells you who is calling before you pick up, used mostly in India.
report.simpleSummary: When an unknown number calls, Truecaller shows the caller's name and warns you if it is spam, like a loan agent or a scammer. It knows the name because hundreds of millions of users share their contacts and report spam numbers. The app is free with ads. You can pay for Premium to remove ads and get extras, and businesses pay to show a verified name and logo when they call or message you.

overview.whatItDoes: Truecaller identifies unknown callers, blocks spam and scam calls and texts, and sorts SMS into inboxes. It makes money from ads in the app, Premium subscriptions, and from businesses that pay to be verified. In 2025 and 2026 it shifted away from ads toward subscriptions and business services.
howItWorks: When you install it, you can share your contacts. These, plus user tags and reports, build a huge crowd-sourced phone book.
When a call comes in, the app looks up the number and shows a name, photo or a red spam warning.
Users can block numbers and report spam, which updates the warning for everyone.
The SMS inbox sorts bank alerts, OTPs, offers and spam into separate tabs.
Businesses pay for 'Verified Business' caller ID, with a green badge, logo and call reason.
Premium users pay to remove ads, see who viewed their profile, and use extras like AI call assistant and contact requests.
overview.valueProposition: For users: know who is calling and avoid scams and wasted time. For businesses: get more calls answered, because people trust a verified name more than an unknown number.

painPoints.pain: Indian phone users get many spam and scam calls every week.
painPoints.howSolved: Red spam warnings and auto-blocking based on reports from millions of users.

painPoints.pain: Unknown numbers could be a delivery, a doctor or a scam, and you cannot tell.
painPoints.howSolved: Caller ID shows the name and sometimes a photo or business tag.

painPoints.pain: SMS inbox is flooded with offers, so bank alerts and OTPs get lost.
painPoints.howSolved: Smart SMS sorts messages into tabs and highlights OTPs and bills.

painPoints.pain: Older or less tech-savvy people are easy targets for fraud.
painPoints.howSolved: Scam alerts and warnings for known fraud numbers, plus family protection features.

painPoints.pain: Businesses cannot get customers to answer calls.
painPoints.howSolved: Verified Business caller ID shows a green badge, logo and reason for call.

painPoints.pain: You miss calls while busy and do not know if they matter.
painPoints.howSolved: AI Assistant can answer, screen and transcribe calls for Premium users.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: A growing business line with steady contracts from banks, apps and delivery firms.

businessModel.summary: Truecaller makes money three ways: ads shown in the app, Premium subscriptions from users, and fees from businesses for verified calls and messages. Ads used to be most of the money, but they fell 12% in Q3 2026, while subscriptions and business revenue grew. Recurring revenue is now almost half of sales.

revenueStreams.detail: Ads after calls and in the app, sold through its own and partner ad systems. Largest stream but shrinking, now under 53% of sales.
Users pay monthly or yearly for an ad-free app and extra features. Up 32% in Q3 2026.
Verified business caller ID and messaging, sold to banks, apps and other firms. Up 14% in Q3 2026.
US subscription calling and texting app with about 1.5 million users, bought in 2026.

businessModel.pricing: Free with ads. In India, Premium costs roughly ₹75 to ₹100 a month or around ₹500 to ₹900 a year, often with discounts, and Gold costs several thousand rupees a year. Prices change and are shown in the app. Business pricing is not public.
costDrivers: Engineering and AI staff, mostly in Stockholm and Bengaluru
Servers to look up billions of calls
Sales staff for business and ads
Google Play and App Store fees on subscriptions
Tax and legal costs, such as the 2026 India tax provision
businessModel.unitEconomics: Truecaller earns very little per user. About SEK 464 million a quarter across 476 million users is roughly SEK 4 (about ₹33) per user per year. But serving one more user costs almost nothing, so margins stay high: about 32 kronor of every 100 is EBITDA. A Premium user in India paying around ₹500 a year is worth about 15 times an ad-only user, and a US Text+ subscriber is worth even more. That is why the company is pushing subscriptions and the US.

howTheyGetUsers: Word of mouth after a scam call scare
Pre-installs and partnerships with Android phone makers
Seeing a friend's phone show caller names
Businesses telling customers to look for their verified badge
whatBringsUsersBack: Every incoming call from an unknown number
SMS inbox used daily for OTPs and bank alerts
Weekly spam stats and protection reports
growth.moat: Truecaller's phone book is built from hundreds of millions of users sharing contacts and reporting spam over 15 years. The more people use it, the more accurate it gets, which is a network effect. A new app would start with no data. The main threat is not another app, but India's government adding caller names at the phone network level.

competitors.name: CNAP (Calling Name Presentation) by Indian telecoms
competitors.positioning: A TRAI-mandated feature showing the caller's KYC-registered name on every phone, being rolled out from 2025 to 2026.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: CNAP shows a registered name but does not label spam or scams. Truecaller argues knowing a name does not solve spam.

competitors.name: Google Phone app
competitors.positioning: Default Android dialer with caller ID and spam protection.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Truecaller has much bigger India-specific spam data and an SMS inbox, but Google's app is already installed.

competitors.name: Telecom spam filters (Airtel, Jio)
competitors.positioning: Network-level AI spam labels like Airtel's spam alert.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Free and built-in, but limited to one network. Truecaller works across all networks.

competitors.name: Apple iPhone call screening
competitors.positioning: iOS features to silence unknown callers and screen calls.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Apple limits what third-party apps can do on iPhone, so Truecaller is weaker on iOS.

competitors.name: Hiya
competitors.positioning: Caller ID and spam protection sold mostly through carriers and phone makers in the US and Europe.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Truecaller is consumer-first and dominant in India; Hiya is B2B through carriers.

northStar.metric: Spam and unknown calls correctly identified per user each month
northStar.why: As a north star metric this shows the core value: fewer wasted or risky calls. It drives retention, ad views and the reasons to pay for Premium.

improvementIdeas.idea: Show 'Truecaller name + CNAP name' together, and highlight when they differ as a fraud warning.
improvementIdeas.problem: CNAP threatens to make basic caller ID free; Truecaller needs to stay more useful.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Users keep Truecaller as the trust layer on top of CNAP.

improvementIdeas.idea: One-tap self-service to fix a wrong name or spam label on your own number, with OTP proof.
improvementIdeas.problem: Users and small businesses complain about wrong tags and hard unlisting.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: False spam rate and support tickets

improvementIdeas.idea: Family Protection plan in India: one payment covers parents' phones with scam alerts sent to the child.
improvementIdeas.problem: Older people are the main scam targets but will not pay.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: New reason to pay, higher revenue per payer.

improvementIdeas.idea: Cap ads at one full-screen ad per day for users with high scam exposure.
improvementIdeas.problem: Ad overload is the top complaint and drives uninstalls.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Better ratings and retention, small short-term ad loss.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Uninstall rate and ad revenue per user

improvementIdeas.idea: Bundle Text+ second numbers with Truecaller Premium in the US.
improvementIdeas.problem: Truecaller is small in rich markets.

pmLessons: A product that gets better as more people use it can win a market, but a government rule can still change the game overnight.
Ads on a free app are fragile. Truecaller moved toward subscriptions and business revenue to make income steadier.
Privacy is part of the product. Building a phone book from users' contacts gave Truecaller its edge but also its biggest complaint.
Platform owners like Apple set the limits of what an app can do, so check your dependencies.

interviewQuestions.question: CNAP will show caller names on every Indian phone. What should Truecaller do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Separate what CNAP solves (names) from what it does not (spam, scams, SMS). Find the value gap, then propose features and a pricing response.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase Truecaller Premium conversion in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users by spam exposure. Look at price, paywall timing, value shown (spam blocked), and family plans. Pick a metric and guardrails.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure the accuracy of spam detection?
interviewQuestions.hint: Define true and false positives. Use user feedback, appeals and sampled audits. Explain the trade-off between blocking more and wrongly blocking real calls.

interviewQuestions.question: Truecaller's ad revenue fell 12%. Diagnose it.
interviewQuestions.hint: Split into users, ad views per user, fill rate and price per ad. Check outside factors like the market and internal ad tech changes.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to protect elderly users from scams.
interviewQuestions.hint: Understand scam types (KYC, electricity bill, digital arrest). Propose alerts, family notifications, and simple UI. Measure scams avoided.
